description: `ui-health validate scenario <name> --json` validates `ui/manifest.json` + overlay against the `scenario-ui-manifest/v1` JSON schema, the on-disk slot directories, and the template-vs-overlay rules; emits a structured `Report` with `Finding`s for schema violations, missing slot directories, unknown slot names in overlays, missing template references, orphan files, and overlapping slot pathPatterns; exits 0 on a clean scenario.

requirements.description: The CLI command `ui-health validate scenario <name> --json` must validate the `ui/manifest.json` file and any overlay configuration against the `scenario-ui-manifest/v1` JSON schema. Validation must check on-disk slot directories exist, enforce template-vs-overlay rules, and detect orphan files and overlapping slot pathPatterns.
requirements.title: Manifest Schema Validation Command

validation.notes: Schema violations in manifest.json produce a Finding with type=SCHEMA_VIOLATION
Missing slot directories produce a Finding with type=MISSING_SLOT_DIRECTORY
Unknown slot names in overlays produce a Finding with type=UNKNOWN_SLOT_NAME
Missing template references produce a Finding with type=MISSING_TEMPLATE_REFERENCE
Orphan files (not referenced by any slot) produce a Finding with type=ORPHAN_FILE
Overlapping slot pathPatterns produce a Finding with type=OVERLAPPING_PATH_PATTERN
A fully valid scenario causes the command to exit with code 0
A scenario with any violation causes the command to exit with a non-zero code
Run `ui-health validate scenario <valid-scenario> --json` and confirm output is a well-formed Report JSON object with zero Findings and exit code 0
Run `ui-health validate scenario <invalid-scenario> --json` with a manifest missing required schema fields and confirm at least one SCHEMA_VIOLATION Finding is present in the JSON output
Run against a scenario with a declared slot whose directory does not exist on disk and confirm MISSING_SLOT_DIRECTORY Finding is emitted
Run against a scenario with an overlay referencing a slot name not present in the manifest and confirm UNKNOWN_SLOT_NAME Finding is emitted
Validation of a scenario with 500 files completes within 5 seconds
All Finding types described in the operational target are representable in the Report output
The --json flag always produces machine-parseable JSON to stdout even when Findings exist

requirements.description: The `ui-health validate` command must emit a structured `Report` object containing a list of `Finding` objects. Each Finding must include at minimum: finding type, affected file or path, a human-readable message, and severity. The Report must be serializable to JSON and must be the sole output to stdout when --json is passed.
requirements.title: Structured Report and Finding Data Model

validation.notes: Report struct serializes to valid JSON with fields: scenario_name, findings[], summary counts
Finding struct includes: type (enum), path, message, severity fields
All defined Finding type enum values are covered by unit tests
Output from `--json` flag parses without error using standard JSON tooling (e.g., jq)
Non-json mode (no flag) emits human-readable text to stdout while still exiting with correct code
Report format is stable and versioned so downstream consumers (e.g., test-genie) can rely on its schema

title: Deterministic manifest validation
